entities.summary:
Decimus Laberius (b. 105 BCE, Ancient Rome) was a journalist or media commentator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Ancient Rome. He is known for his works in the fields of poets & playwrights.


Decimus Laberius was a prominent figure in the Roman literary scene, contributing to the development of satire and social commentary. His writings often critiqued the excesses of the Roman elite, reflecting the societal tensions of the time.


Laberius' legacy can be seen in the work of later Roman writers, such as Juvenal and Martial, who continued his tradition of satire and social commentary.


The historian Suetonius credited Laberius with helping to shape the literary style of the Roman satirist, noting that Laberius' work 'was the first to establish the style of satire that was to be emulated for centuries to come.'


Today, Decimus Laberius is recognized as a key figure in the history of Roman literature, his contributions to the development of satire and social commentary continuing to influence writers and scholars to this day.
